summary: An intra-African migrant that arrives to breed in the rainy season. The sexes are alike in plumage: dark grey head, upper parts and wings, pale grey throat and breast, and a white belly barred dark grey. The tail is dark grey, fully barred, with a white tip, and the upper tail coverts are grey. The male eye is yellow and the female eye is light brown. The bill is yellow, tipped black or horn, and the legs are yellowish. The male calls coo-coo, with the second note higher and louder. The female gives a bubbling kwik-kwik-kwik. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Cuckoo has incompletely barred outer tail feathers. African Cuckoo has complete tail barring. Both have grey upper tail coverts.
Red-chested Cuckoo has a broad russet upper breast. African Cuckoo has a pale grey throat and breast.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

viewNotes.note: Dark grey above, pale grey on the throat and breast, and a barred white belly. The eye is yellow.
Pale grey breast and a barred white belly. The bill is yellow with a dark tip.
Dark grey upper parts and grey upper tail coverts. The tail is fully barred and white-tipped.
The flight is dashing and looks like a bird of prey. Barred underwings were not named in the text.
Barred white belly and pale grey breast.

calls.description: A coo-coo, the second note higher and louder than the first. The female utters a bubbling kwik-kwik-kwik, which was not given a separate file. Grade A song from Mutinondo, Zambia. The filename names African Cuckoo and the song.
